result.headline: Vodafone is the likely best network because its site 1.4 km north has a clear line of sight, while EE and Three signals are likely weakened by hills [los_vodafone][los_ee][los_three].
result.explanation: Vodafone’s nearest confirmed site is 1.4 km north and the direct line clears the ground by at least 2 m, so terrain does not block it [los_vodafone]. EE and Three sites are 6.5 km south-east, and terrain rises 137 m above the direct line 2.0 km away, likely weakening their signals [los_ee][los_three]. The nearest mast overall is only 0.5 km west, but its operator is unknown [nearest_site]. Measured speeds nearby are low (about 14 Mbps) compared with the UK median of 103 Mbps [speed_cell], which is consistent with a weak signal at this location. Only Vodafone has confirmed sites within 5 km, and no O2 site was found within 10 km, though crowd-sourced site data is incomplete so this is not certain [operators_5km][no_site_o2].

rule_based.label: Based on data, not yet reviewed by agents
rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: Likely best network here: Vodafone, with a clear line of sight to a site 1.4 km north (confirmed by Ofcom's licence register). No site identified in our data for O2.

operators.note: No O2 site identified in our data within 10 km (not the same as no coverage).

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level, not exact for this address.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

All citations exist and agree. No unchecked alternatives could change the ranking.
